The Mergado API is based on REST principles. The request/response format is JSON. This documentation is a part of [Mergado Docs](https://mergado.github.io/docs/intro/the-basics.html). ## 📋 Changelog
Show changelog history
### 2026-10-02 #### Changed * Endpoint `GET /me/` - `mfa_enabled` is served only with `include_additional_fields=true`, because it costs a request to Accounts. When Accounts is unavailable or fails, the field is left out instead of failing the whole request. Older versions (from `2026-06-08`) keep serving it always, as `null` when Accounts fails. ### 2026-09-04 #### Changed * Endpoint `PATCH /projects/{id}/` - `turned_off` is no longer a writable field. A project is turned on and off in the Mergado app, not through the API, so the field is now ignored the same way as any other field the endpoint does not accept: a body carrying it still answers `200` and the project keeps the state it had. It is served on read as before. A value that is not a JSON boolean is no longer refused with `400` either, because the field is not validated at all any more. * Endpoint `POST /shops/{id}/projects/` - The new project is turned on before the response is written, so `turned_off` in the `201` body is now `false`. It used to be `true`, because the project was stored turned off and a background task turned it on a moment later. ### 2026-09-02 #### Changed * Endpoints `POST /projects/{id}/rules/` and `PATCH /rules/{id}/` - Both now accept a `schedule` object limiting when the rule is allowed to apply - the same schedule the Mergado UI offers. It carries `enabled`, an inclusive `date_from`/`date_until` range, the `apply_before`/`apply_after` policies deciding whether the rule applies outside that range, and `weekdays`, mapping ISO-8601 weekday indexes (1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday) to the hours (0-23) the rule applies at. **`weekdays` must name whole 4-hour blocks** (`0-3`, `4-7`, `8-11`, `12-15`, `16-19`, `20-23`), which is the granularity the Mergado UI edits the schedule in - a partial block (e.g. `[1, 2]`) is rejected with 400, because opening and saving such a schedule in the UI would silently widen or drop it. A schedule can only ever block a rule that would otherwise apply, it never resumes a paused one. On `PATCH` an omitted `schedule` leaves the existing one untouched, while an explicit `null` removes it. Rules of type `hiding` never honour a schedule, so sending one for them is rejected, and converting a rule into a `hiding` rule drops the schedule it had. * Endpoints `POST /projects/{id}/rules/` and `PATCH /rules/{id}/` - Query references inside `data` are now validated. Rule types that point at queries from their own payload (`batch_rewriting` via `rows[].query_id`, `batch_set_datetime` via `rows[].query_ids`) are rejected with 400 naming the offending IDs when a referenced query does not exist or belongs to another project. Previously an unknown ID either ended as a 500 (`batch_rewriting`, which is backed by a foreign key) or was stored as a dangling reference without any error (`batch_set_datetime`). This is the same check `queries` at the top level of the request has always had. * Field `schedule` on `GET /rules/{id}/`, `GET /projects/{id}/rules/` and the `POST`/`PATCH` rule responses - Rule responses now carry the stored schedule, or `null` when the rule has none. * Endpoints `PATCH /projects/{id}/products/` and `PATCH /queries/{id}/products/` - Reject `is_hidden` and `manual_changes` with 400 instead of silently ignoring them; both are per-product operations, use `PATCH /products/{id}/` for them. * Parameter `values_to_extract` on `GET`/`POST /projects/{id}/products/` and `GET /queries/{id}/products/` - The response now serves the extracted values **instead of** the `data` field carrying the product's whole element tree, which it used to serve next to them. Extracting values is how a caller says which values it needs, so answering with every element of every product anyway defeated the point - on a large feed that tree is the bulk of the response. A caller that wants both names `data` in the `fields` parameter (`?fields=data,extracted_values`), which is also how the smaller response could be asked for before. Every version of these endpoints that accepts `values_to_extract` answers this way, not only the current one - serving the tree anyway was the bug, not the contract. * Endpoint `GET /projects/{id}/elements/` - Every level of the tree is now an object with an `elements` and an `attributes` mapping instead of one mapping keyed by name. An element and an attribute of one parent may share a name, and keying both by that name alone meant whichever came second overwrote the first, so one of the two was missing from the response entirely. Each mapping is keyed by plain name and ordered by `order` within its own group - elements and attributes are numbered independently, so both sequences start at 1. Older versions of the endpoint answer as they did before, with the collision. #### Added * Fields `is_hidden_set_manually` and `output_cdata` on `GET /projects/{id}/elements/`, `GET /elements/{id}/`, `POST /projects/{id}/elements/` and `PATCH /elements/{id}/` - Whether the element was hidden by a person rather than by the import, and whether its value is written into the output feed wrapped in CDATA. Both belong to the element's setup and were the only part of it the API did not serve. Both are optional on write and default to `false`. * Field `autohide_new_products` on `GET /projects/{id}/` and `GET /shops/{id}/projects/` - Whether newly imported products are hidden until somebody authorizes them. The endpoint has accepted it on write for a while but never served it back. * Field `encoding` on `GET /projects/{id}/` and `GET /shops/{id}/projects/` - The encoding the input feed is read with, or `null` when the import detects it from the feed itself (which is the usual case). * Field `namespaces` on `GET /users/{user_id}/formats/{format_id}` - The XML namespaces a custom format declares, each with its `prefix` and `uri`. Empty for a format that is not XML or declares none. A format that does declare them cannot be rebuilt anywhere else without them. * Field `upload_control` in the `data` of `data_import` rules - A data import that reads an uploaded file rather than a URL now says so with `uploaded_filename` and `uploaded_size`. Sending `upload_control.uploaded_data` on `POST`/`PATCH` stores the file, which is the only way to give such a rule its file through the API. * Parameter `include_additional_fields` on `GET /rules/{id}/` and `GET /projects/{id}/rules/` - Adds `upload_control.uploaded_data` - the content of a data import's uploaded file - to the response. **It is left out unless this is set to `true`**, because a data import may carry up to 25 MB of it and the rule listing is one of the busiest endpoints of the API. Anything other than `true`/`false` is rejected with 400. A file over 25 MB - the same limit the UI enforces - is rejected with 400 on write, rather than stored and refused later, and changing a rule's `type` away from `data_import`, or switching its `data_source_type` to `url`, deletes the file it was carrying. * Endpoint `PATCH /products/{id}/` - Besides `is_dirty` it now also hides a single product manually (`is_hidden`) and sets element values by hand (`manual_changes`) - the same two operations the Mergado UI offers on a product. Only the fields present in the request body are changed. `manual_changes` is merged into the manual values the product already has, `"value": null` removes one. Both need write access to the project and schedule a regeneration of it. * Fields `is_hidden`, `is_hidden_by_rule`, `is_hidden_manually` and `manual_changes` on `GET /products/{id}/` - Tell whether the product is left out of the output feed (and whether that is because of a hiding rule, because it was hidden manually, or both) and list the element values set manually for it. Every manual change carries `is_applied`, which is `false` until the project is regenerated. Older versions of the endpoint answer as they did before, without these fields. * Parameter `include_additional_fields` on `GET`/`POST /projects/{id}/products/` and `GET /queries/{id}/products/` - Adds the four fields above to a product list. **They are left out unless this is set to `true`**, because building them costs queries the rest of the response does not need - the manual state lives in tables of its own and the hiding rules of the project have to be evaluated for it. Product lists are the busiest endpoints of the API, so a caller that does not need the state is not made to pay for it. Anything other than `true`/`false` is rejected with 400. ### 2026-08-19 #### Changed * Endpoint `PATCH /projects/{id}/` - Besides `is_dirty` it now also updates `name`, `shop_id` (moves the project to another shop), `url`, `autohide_new_products` and `turned_off` (turns the project on/off). Only the fields present in the request body are changed, any other field is ignored as before. #### Added * Endpoint `POST /elements/parse` - Parses a CSV/XML data file and returns the elements it contains, without needing a project. The response has the same nested shape as `GET /projects/{id}/elements/` and adds `path`, `count` and `example` for every element, so a client can offer the file's elements to the user before anything is created in Mergado. * Endpoint `POST /projects/{id}/duplicate/` - Duplicates a project into the same shop or, with `shop_id`, into another one. Returns the newly created project id. ### 2026-08-14 #### Added * Endpoint `/projects/{id}/tracing/products/` (`GET`, `POST`) - Lists/marks products for rule-apply tracing (the "representative sample" mechanism). * Endpoint `GET /projects/{id}/tracing/products/changes/` - Rule-apply changes recorded for the project's traced products. * Endpoint `DELETE /projects/{id}/tracing/products/{product_id}/` - Unmarks a single traced product. * Endpoint `POST /projects/{id}/tracing/apply/` - Triggers a rule apply run scoped to only the project's traced products; returns the new apply log. ### 2026-08-10 #### Added * Endpoint `/shops/{id}/kaufland/proxy/{path}` * Connection `kaufland.de` to `GET /shops/{id}/info/` - Fields: `client_key` ### 2026-08-05 #### Added * Endpoint `GET /users/{user_identifier}/permissions/app` - Lists all currently enabled apps the user has access to - apps enabled for the user themselves, for any e-shop they own or have a permission for, and for the active projects of those e-shops. Every item contains `app_name`, the subject the app is enabled for (`subject_type`, `subject_id`) and the user's `role` in it. ### 2026-07-22 #### Changed * Field `pairing_elements` on `GET /projects/{id}/`, `PATCH /projects/{id}/`, `GET /shops/{id}/projects/` and `POST /shops/{id}/projects/` - Now exchanged as an array of element paths (`["ITEM_ID", "CODE"]`) instead of a single comma-separated string. Older versions keep receiving/accepting the string. #### Added * Endpoint `/apps/{app_full_name}/mcp` (`POST`, `GET`) - Streaming proxy to a registered app's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over the Streamable HTTP transport. `POST` forwards JSON-RPC messages; `GET` opens an SSE stream. Requests are relayed to the app's `mcp_url` with a short-lived, scope-intersected app-scoped JWT. ### 2026-06-08 #### Changed * Endpoint `GET /notifications/{id}/` - Field `channels` replaced by `statuses` array. Each entry contains `status_id`, `channel`, `user_id`, and `resolved_at` (datetime|null). * Endpoint `GET /users/{user_identifier}/notifications/` - Field `channels` replaced by the same `statuses` array format as `GET /notifications/{id}/`. - `status_id` (string): ID of the `NotificationStatus` record; use it to call `PATCH /notifications/{id}/status/{status_id}/`. #### Added * Endpoint `/notifications/{id}/status/{status_id}/` ### 2026-06-08 #### Changed * Endpoint `GET /me/` - Added field: `mfa_enabled` (boolean, nullable) — sourced live from Accounts ### 2026-05-18 #### Added * Endpoint `/shops/{id}/google/search_console/proxy/{path}` * Connection `google_search_console` to `GET /shops/{id}/info/` - Fields: `site_url` ### 2026-05-13 #### Added * Endpoint `/shops/{id}/google/ads/proxy/{path}` * Endpoint `/shops/{id}/google/spreadsheets/proxy/{path}` * Connection `google_ads` to `GET /shops/{id}/info/` - Fields: `customer_id`, `customer_name`, `mcc_id` ### 2026-03-19 ### 2026-05-31 #### Added * Endpoint `POST /shops/` - Create a new e-shop * Endpoint `POST /shops/{id}/projects/` - Create a new project for a shop ### 2025-12-03 #### Changed * Endpoint GET `/shops/{id}/info` - Removed obsolete connections. - Removed vague fields: `currency`, `status`, `valid_credentials` and `error` from connections. #### Added * Endpoint `/shops/{id}/{connection}/validate` ### 2025-09-24 #### Added * Endpoint `/shops/{id}/unas/proxy/{path}` ### 2025-09-24 #### Changed * Endpoint `POST /shops/{id}/notifications/` - Field `scope` now receives and returns `'eshop'|'owner'` instead of `'shop'|'owner'`. - Returned JSON contains new fields: `event`, `data`. - Success response no longer contains `Location` header. * Endpoint `GET /notifications/{id}/` - Now requires scope `user.notify.read`. - **Stricter access control** - Returned JSON contains new fields: `event`, `data`. * Endpoint `GET /users/{user_identifier}/notifications/` - Structure for each notification in response's `data` list is now the same as what `GET /notifications/{id}/` returns. * Endpoint `POST /users/{user_identifier}/notifications/` - Success response no longer contains `Location` header. ### 2025-09-24 #### Added * Endpoint `/shops/{id}/eshop-rychle/proxy/{path}` ### 2025-08-22 #### Added * Endpoint `/shops/{id}/heureka/proxy/{path}` * Field `api_enabled` to `/shops//info` ### 2025-03-23 #### Added * `element_path` and `is_output` parameter for `/projects/{id}/elements/values` and `/projects/{id}/elements/values` endpoints ### 2025-02-13 #### Added * `is_hidden` parameter for `projects/{id}/products/` and `/queries/{id}/products/` endpoints ### 2025-01-09 #### Changed * Renamed the fields `xml_changed_at` and `xml_synced_at` to `data_changed_at` and `data_synced_at` in the `projects/id/` endpoint ### 2024-09-11 #### Added * `invoicing_validity_date`, `avatars`, and `phone` fields to the `/users/` and `/users/{id}/` endpoints, these endpoints are now also accessible with offline tokens * **POST** method for `/products/{id}/` endpoint to set the `is_dirty` field ### 2024-07-24 #### Added * `in_testing_mode` field in `/shops/{id}/projects/` and `/projects/{id}/` endpoints #### Removed * `created_at` field in `/projects/{id}/products/`, `/products/{id}/` and `/queries/{id}/products/` endpoints ### 2024-01-25 #### Added * `values_to_extract` parameter for `/queries/{id}/products/` endpoint ### 2023-10-10 #### Added * `values_to_extract` parameter for `projects/{id}/products/` endpoint ### 2022-09-14 #### Added * Endpoint `/formats/{format_id}` * Endpoint `/formats/{format_id}/specification` #### Changed * Versioning * Endpoint `/projects/{id}/elements` * Endpoint `/elements/{id}` * Endpoint `/projects/{id}/products` * Endpoint `/products/{id}` * Endpoint `/queries/{id}/products`
## Requests The recommended encoding of all requests is UTF-8. Requests must be made over **HTTPS** and all endpoints start with `https://api.mergado.com/`. Note that almost all API endpoints require [OAuth 2.0 authentication](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749). ### Allowed HTTPs requests | Method | Description | |--------|----------------------------------------------| | GET | Retrieves a resource or a list of resources. | | POST | Creates or updates a resource. | | PATCH | Updates a resource. | | DELETE | Deletes a resource. | ### Additional GET parameters | Parameter | Example | Description | |------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------| | **fields** | `?fields=uri,shop.id` | Only fields `uri` and `id` nested in `shop` will be returned in the given example. It works also for arrays of results - filter is applied to all their items, one by one. | | **limit**, **offset** | `?limit=5&offset=2` | Works for arrays only. It is for paging the results. In the example, 2 results from the beginning are skipped and only 5 following items are returned. The default limit for every array result is 10 items. | | **date** | `?date=2015-12-24` | Works only for some special endpoints. In the example, it will return results corresponding only to Christmas Eve in 2015. | **filter** | `?filter=[{"field": "to", "op": ">=", "value": "2021-08-08T13:00:00"}]` | Filters the result. Parameter accepts a valid JSON list with at least one filter. Returned objects meet conditions for all filters. Supported operators are: `=`, `!=`, `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `~` (regexp), `in`. Only numbers and timestamps in ISO 8601 format can be ordinally compared. Missing values in timestamps will be supplemented by the lowest possible values, eg `"2015-12-24"` equals `"2015-12-24T00:00:00+00:00"`. Checks for `null` values is possible with `=` and `!=`. For other operators the comparison with `null` will always fail. Only non-nested fields are expected. | | **order_by** | `?order_by=validator,-verdict` | Orders the result in ascending or descending order. | | filter_by | `?filter_by={"item_id__in":["123456789"]}` | **!! DEPRECATED !!** Used only for Feed Audit and Statistics. Filters the result. You can also append field name with `__in`, i.e. filter results by enumerating all values of a field, for example `item_id__in` expects list of possible ITEM_IDs. | | **values_to_extract** | `?values_to_extract=["ITEM_ID", "PARAM | PARAM_NAME", "Variable"]` | The functionality is limited to the `List Products` endpoint. You can specify a list of element paths or variable names for which the endpoint will return a list of values in a new field called `extracted_values`. The `data` field, carrying every element of the product, is **left out** of such a response - the extracted values are what the caller asked for. Add `data` to the `fields` parameter to get both. | | **mql** | `?mql=PRICE_VAT < 100` | The functionality is limited to the `List Products` endpoints. Parameter allows filtering products based on [MQL](https://mergado.github.io/docs/apps/rules-and-queries.html) query. | | **is_hidden** | `?is_hidden=false` | The functionality is limited to the `List Products` endpoints. Parameter allows filtering products based on their visibility status. | | **element_path** | `?element_path=GIFT { NO_ATTR = "sleva 20%" } | @ID` | The functionality is limited to the `Element values` endpoints. Parameter allows filtering element values based on their `element path.`| | **is_output** | `?is_output=true` | The function is limited to `Element Values` endpoints. The parameter allows you to specify whether to return the input or output values ​​of the element.`| #### Encoding All special characters in additional GET parameter values must be URL-encoded (also known as percent-encoding). ### Typical Server Responses | Code | Status | Description | |------|--------------------|-------------| | 200 | OK | The request was successful (some API calls may return 201 instead). In case of arrays, `total_results` or `after` is returned as part of the envelope (together with `limit` and `offset`). It corresponds to the total amount of resources that match the request. | | 201 | Created | The request was successful and a resource was created. | | 204 | No Content | The request was successful but there is no representation to return (that is, the response is empty). | | 400 | Bad Request | The request could not be understood or was missing required parameters. | | 401 | Unauthorized | Authentication failed or user does not have permissions for the requested operation. | | 403 | Forbidden | Access denied. | | 404 | Not Found | Resource was not found. | | 405 | Method Not Allowed | Requested method is not supported for the specified resource. | | 409 | Conflict | Resource already exists and could not be created. | ## OAuth 2.0 To access Mergado API, clients (e.g. an application) are required to authenticate with [OAuth 2.0](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749). Each application is required to have its OAuth credentials which can be obtained from the Mergado [developers center](https://developers.mergado.com) (during registeration of your application, a client ID and a secret key is assigned to your application). * [Basics of OAuth 2.0 in Mergado Apps](http://mergado.github.io/docs/api/authorization.html) * [List of all OAuth scopes](http://mergado.github.io/docs/api/oauth-scopes.html) ### Online and offline access tokens Mergado API distinguishes between situations where your Mergado platform app accesses API **on behalf of some specific Mergado user** and where the app is accessing API **on behalf of the app itself**. Access tokens bound to some specific user ID are called ***online*** tokens. Access tokens bound only to the app itself are called ***offline*** tokens. ## Versioning Versioning is implemented using the `use-mergado-api-version` header. The valid syntax is: `use-mergado-api-version`: "YYYY-MM-DD", eg. `use-mergado-api-version`: "2022-01-19". For any endpoint, * in case of a date X is specified in the `use-mergado-api-version` header, and * there exists only one endpoint version, then the default endpoint version will be used, * there exist endpoint versions valid until dates A and B, and the newest version C, and A < B < X < C holds, then the newest version of the endpoint C will be used, * there exist only endpoint versions valid until the dates A and B, and A < B < X holds (i.e. there is no newest version), then the error 404 will be returned, * in case of there is no date specified in the `use-mergado-api-version` header, the endpoint valid on 2020-09-07 will be used. Note that all request and response examples match the latest version.

Verifies whether the caller (identified by the provided token) has read or write access to one or more target entities.

When the token is a JWT with an `aud` field (issued by the app proxy), a **dual access check** is enforced: both the caller and the target app must have independent access to the requested entity.

Each check in the request specifies an `entity_type` (`shop` or `project`), an `entity_id`, and an optional `access` level (`read` or `write`). If `access` is omitted, the endpoint determines the maximum access level.

For more details, see the [Cross-Platform Communication documentation](https://mergado.github.io/docs/apps/cross-platform-communication.html).

**Attributes:**
* **id (string):** ID of the log.
* **duration (number):** How long the action took.
* **started_at (string):** When the action started.
* **finished_at (string):** When the action ended.
* **rules (array):** List of rules involved in the action.
* **user_id (string):** ID of the user who started the action.
* **applied_to_all_items (boolean):** Whether the action has been performed on all products.
* **status (string):** Result of the action. One of `in_progress` (still running),
  `success` (finished, no errors nor warnings), `warning` (finished, no errors but
  with warnings), `failure` (finished with errors). Filterable via `?filter=`.
* **errors (array):** List of errors that occurred during the action. Each item has
  `type` and `message`. Empty array when there are none.
* **warnings (array):** List of warnings that occurred during the action. Each item
  has `type`, `data` (JSON-encoded warning details) and `product_ids` (list of
  affected product IDs). Empty array when there are none.

get.description:
Transparent proxy to a registered app's API. Any HTTP request sent to this endpoint is intercepted by Mergado, which:

1. Verifies that the caller holds a valid Mergado API token.
2. Computes the scope intersection between the caller's scopes and the target app's registered scopes.
3. Generates a short-lived JWT token containing the caller's identity, intersected scopes, and the target app as `aud` (audience).
4. Forwards the request to the target app's configured `api_url` with the JWT in the `Authorization` header.

The JWT token contains the following fields:
- `entity_id` — ID of the entity making the request.
- `entity_type` — Type of the entity: `user`, `shop`, or `project`.
- `scopes` — Intersection of the caller's OAuth scopes and the target app's scopes.
- `aud` — Full name of the target app (audience).
- `exp` — Expiration timestamp (~5 minutes).

All HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) are supported. Query parameters, headers, and request body are forwarded unchanged.

For more details, see the [Cross-Platform Communication documentation](https://mergado.github.io/docs/apps/cross-platform-communication.html).

post.description:
Authenticated proxy to a registered app's **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** server, speaking the MCP *Streamable HTTP* transport. It shares the app-proxy trust model: the caller authenticates with a Mergado API token and Mergado forwards the request to the app's configured `mcp_url` using a freshly minted, app-scoped JWT - the only credential ever seen by the app. Mergado:

1. Verifies that the caller holds a valid Mergado API token.
2. Computes the scope intersection between the caller's scopes and the target app's registered scopes.
3. Generates a short-lived JWT containing the caller's identity, intersected scopes, and the target app as `aud` (audience).
4. Forwards the request to the app's `mcp_url` with the JWT in the `Authorization` header and streams the response body back to the client without buffering.

The JWT token contains the following fields:
- `entity_id` - ID of the entity making the request.
- `entity_type` - Type of the entity: `user`, `shop`, or `project`.
- `scopes` - Intersection of the caller's OAuth scopes and the target app's scopes.
- `aud` - Full name of the target app (audience).
- `exp` - Expiration timestamp (~5 minutes).

Only **POST** and **GET** are supported (any other verb returns `405`):
- **POST** - send one or more JSON-RPC messages to the app. The app may answer with a single JSON document, an empty `202 Accepted` (for notifications/responses) or an SSE stream of messages.
- **GET** - open a long-lived SSE stream to receive server-initiated messages (the connection channel).

The MCP transport headers `Mcp-Session-Id`, `MCP-Protocol-Version` and `Last-Event-ID` are forwarded in both directions so session continuity, protocol negotiation and stream resumption work end to end. For SSE responses Mergado disables intermediary buffering (`X-Accel-Buffering: no`) so events reach the client in real time.

For more details, see the [Cross-Platform Communication documentation](https://mergado.github.io/docs/apps/cross-platform-communication.html).

**Experimental** - this endpoint is experimental and may change or be removed without notice.

Parses a CSV or XML data file and returns the elements it contains, without needing a project
in Mergado. Meant for preparing a data import (typically an AI agent over MCP) - the elements
of a file can be offered to the user before anything is created.

The file is downloaded from `url` and parsed synchronously, so the elements are in the
response - there is nothing to poll. The format is detected from the content, not from the

* `order` - position among its siblings, in document order
* `is_attribute` - whether it is an XML attribute (attributes are parsed as separate
  elements and their key is prefixed with `@`)

* `count` - how many times it occurs in the file
* `example` - the first value found, useful for deciding what the element holds
* `children` - nested elements, present only when the element wraps something

patch.description:
Updates a single product. Only the fields present in the request body are
changed, everything else is left as it is.

**`is_dirty`** forces Mergado to refresh the product (apply rules) during the next
(lazy) rebuild. For optimization reasons, this field is not returned in the response,
and whether the product has already been applied can be checked in the logs
at `/projects/<id>/applylogs/`. Nevertheless, it is acceptable to mark the product
as dirty without prior checking to see if it is even necessary.

**`is_hidden`** hides the product manually, i.e. leaves it out of the output feed
regardless of the project's rules (`true`), or takes that manual hiding back (`false`).
This is the very same operation as the hide/show button in the Mergado UI, and it is
independent of the project's hiding rules - a product matched by a hiding rule stays
hidden even when `is_hidden` is set to `false`. To hide a whole group of products,
create a rule of type `hiding` instead.

**`manual_changes`** sets element values by hand, on top of what the rules compute.
Every item is an object with an `element_path` and a `value`:

+ the items are merged into what the product already has - an element path that is
not mentioned keeps its manual value,

+ `"value": null` removes the manual value of that element path, so the value computed
by the rules comes back,

+ the element path has to exist in the project (see `GET /projects/{id}/elements/`)
and is stored normalized, so the same change is seen by the Mergado UI,

+ an element path that does not say which value it means matches every value of
that element and only the **first** one is changed the normalized path returned
back names the position that was taken. Spell out `@@POSITION` to change any other
value - each of them is a manual change of its own,

+ the same element path must not be present twice in one request.

Both `is_hidden` and `manual_changes` only take effect in the output feed once the
project is regenerated, which this endpoint schedules on its own. Until then, the
affected manual changes are returned with `"is_applied": false`.

Hiding and manual values are per-product operations: the bulk endpoints
`PATCH /projects/{id}/products/` and `PATCH /queries/{id}/products/` reject them
with 400 instead of silently ignoring them.

**OAuth2 Scope:** `project.products.write`. Hiding a product and changing its values
additionally requires write access to the project itself.

**PATCH** `https://api.mergado.com/products/id/`

is_dirty.description: Flags the product to have the rules applied to it during the next rebuild.

is_hidden.description: Hides the product manually (true) or takes the manual hiding back (false). Products hidden by a hiding rule are not affected.

manual_changes.description: Element values to set by hand. Merged into the manual values the product already has; a null value removes one.

element_path.description: Element path of the value to change. The element has to exist in the project. A path matching more than one value changes the first of them - name the `@@POSITION` to reach another.

value.description: The value to set, or null to remove the manual value of this element path.

post.description:
Creates a new rule inside the specified project. At least one query must be supplied (e.g. the ID of the ♥ALLPRODUCTS♥ query).

Priority can be set in two ways:
- **placement** - place the rule relative to an existing rule via `placement.before` / `placement.after`.
- **priority** - set an explicit numeric value. If the value is already taken the server adjusts to the
  next free slot.

`placement` takes precedence over `priority`. If neither is provided for rule types that require priority,
a 400 is returned.

The `data` field must match the schema registered for the rule type. Call `GET /rules/definitions/{rule_type}/`
to retrieve the full JSON Schema for the expected payload. Positions within multi-row data (e.g. `batch_rewriting`)
are assigned automatically when sent as `null` and preserved when provided explicitly.

Some rule types reference queries from within `data` itself - `batch_rewriting` through `rows[].query_id`,
`batch_param` through `rows[].queries` and `batch_set_datetime` through `rows[].query_ids`. Those IDs must belong
to queries of the same project, exactly like the IDs in the top-level `queries` field; a query that does not
exist or lives in another project is rejected with 400 naming the offending IDs. The rule is also assigned to
every such query, on top of the queries given in `queries`, so they also appear in the rule's `queries`.
When `data` (or the rule type) changes and `queries` is not sent, queries only the previous `data` referenced
are unassigned again; if that would leave the rule without any query, the update is rejected with 400.

**Note:** The maximum length of `name` is 100 characters. Special characters are not allowed.

**OAuth2 Scope:** `project.rules.write`

**POST** `https://api.mergado.com/projects/id/rules/`

type.description: Rule type identifier (e.g. 'rewriting', 'calc', 'batch_rewriting'). Must have a registered schema.

name.description: Human-readable label. Max 100 characters, no special characters.

schedule.description: Schedule limiting when the rule may apply. Omit to create the rule without a schedule. Not supported by `hiding` rules.

enabled.description: When false the schedule is stored but has no effect.

date_from.description: First day the weekday schedule is in effect (inclusive).

date_until.description: Last day the weekday schedule is in effect (inclusive).

apply_before.description: Whether the rule applies on days before `date_from`.

apply_after.description: Whether the rule applies on days after `date_until`.

weekdays.description: Hours (0-23) the rule applies at, keyed by ISO-8601 weekday index (1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday). Hours must cover whole 4-hour blocks (0-3, 4-7, 8-11, 12-15, 16-19, 20-23) - these are the blocks the Mergado UI edits the schedule in, and saving the schedule there rewrites the whole weekday, so a schedule naming only part of a block could not survive being opened and saved in the UI. A partial block is rejected with 400.

post.description:
**Experimental** - this endpoint is experimental and may change or be removed without notice.

Creates a new project for the specified eshop.

The feed URL is validated for scheme (`http`, `https`, `sftp`). For `http`/`https` URLs
a reachability pre-check is performed - the endpoint returns `422` if the server responds
with `401`, `403`, `404`, `408` or any `5xx` status code. Timeouts and connection errors
are treated as non-fatal and do not block project creation.

`input_format` and `output_format` are required and must be valid Mergado format IDs
(native or custom). When they differ, a format-converter rule is automatically inserted.
The project is turned on before the response is written, so the `201` body already reports
it as running. Its schedule and its first feed synchronisation are set up in the background
afterwards.

A project without both formats, or without a pairing element, is one that cannot work:
the web frontend resolves both formats for every page it renders for the project, and
an import with nothing to pair on matches no products. Both are therefore refused with
`400` rather than stored.

**Other constraints:**
* `name` - required, max 100 characters, must be unique within the shop
* `url` - required, max length enforced, scheme must be `http`, `https`, or `sftp`
* `input_format` / `output_format` - required, must be a valid native or custom format ID
* `pairing_elements` - required, between 1 and 4 elements. Stored as one comma-separated
  value (max 250 characters); a comma inside `[...]` belongs to the element rather than
  separating two of them. The pairing engine reads at most 4, so more are refused rather
  than stored and ignored.
* `autohide_new_products` - optional, default `false`

**OAuth2 Scope:** `shop.projects.write`

**Product Logic & Filtering:**
A product represents one item currently present in an XML feed.
* **Extracted Values:** If the `values_to_extract` parameter is provided, the response will include the `extracted_values` field and leave out the `data` field with the product's whole element tree (add `data` to the `fields` parameter to get both). Otherwise, `extracted_values` is omitted.
* **MQL Filtering:** You can filter products using the `mql` parameter in a `GET` request. For complex queries that exceed URL limits, use a `POST` request with the `mql` value in the body.
* **Visibility (is_hidden):** * `true` – Returns only hidden products.
    * `false` – Returns only non-hidden products.
    * `null` (or omitted) – Returns all products.

tags.description:
An Audit represents a validation process of an XML feed. It checks for format correctness, missing attributes, and other common errors. 
**Webhook Integration:** If a `webhook_url` is provided, Mergado will send an asynchronous POST request with the results once the processing is complete. Audit of product feed.

- Issues are checks with non-ok verdicts. Some issues are feed-wide, so
  they are bound only to an audit resource. Most issues are product-specific,
  so they are bound to audit and also to product resource.

- Every validator provides specific additional info to check. It is accessible
  in `info` field of issues and it can have various forms - its schema is
  validator-dependent.

- Web hook URL is requested with POST (audit's JSON resource sent in data)
  right in the moment when audit is finished.

- Progress is raised by every check, there is no information about *total*
  number of progress units.

- Feed type is optional. In case it's missing, it is detected before audit
  starts.

- Error field of audits and issues has nothing to do with checking itself -
  is is used only in case mergado3 application fails and raises an exception.
  This generic error field is rather for debugging API than for being consumed
  by API clients.

- Product's data is parsed and saved just *as is* into data field. No semantic
  analysis is performed, validators take it raw and do whatever they want
  with it. This means the data field also has no fixed schema.

- Audits can be scheduled.
tags.name: Feed Audits

The API is available to e-shops which use Kaufland Marketplace and fulfill API access conditions. The API is a RESTful JSON API. You can find more information about the API in the official documentation. Base URL for the Kaufland Marketplace Seller API is https://sellerapi.kaufland.com/v2/. This endpoint works as a proxy.

**Partner credentials override**

By default, requests are signed with Mergado's own Kaufland partner credentials. An app may instead sign the partner part of the request itself, with its own Kaufland partner secret key, by sending three headers: `Shop-Partner-Client-Key`, `Shop-Partner-Signature`, and `Shop-Timestamp`. All three must be present together, or none at all — a partial set is rejected with `400`.

`Shop-Partner-Signature` must be computed over the **upstream Kaufland URL**, not this proxy's URL — that is, `https://sellerapi.kaufland.com/v2/{path}` with the exact same query string as the request sent to this endpoint, in the same parameter order. A mismatch in parameter order, encoding, or a missing/extra trailing slash results in a `403` from Kaufland with no further explanation, since Mergado forwards the supplied signature as-is without validating it itself.

Example: a `GET` request sent to
`https://api.mergado.com/shops/42/kaufland/proxy/units/?limit=5&status=active`
must be signed as if it were sent directly to
`https://sellerapi.kaufland.com/v2/units/?limit=5&status=active`
— `{path}` (`units/`) and the query string (`limit=5&status=active`) are appended, unchanged, to `https://sellerapi.kaufland.com/v2/`.
